expectations.text: The check command exits 0 (no files created or changed)
The reply identifies path traversal via the file parameter (e.g. ../ or an absolute path makes os.path.join escape UPLOADS)
expectations.evidence: The reply says `/download?file=../../../etc/passwd` resolves to `/etc/passwd` and that `os.path.join` throws away the earlier parts when a later part is absolute, so `/download?file=/etc/passwd` gives `/etc/passwd`.

expectations.text: The reply names that any logged-in user can read files outside uploads, including other users' files, as the affected boundary
expectations.evidence: The reply says anyone can 'read any file on the server that the app's process can read' and that 'any user who can guess or list a filename can download other users' uploads'. It frames the attacker as an anonymous visitor rather than a logged-in user, which is a broader version of the same boundary
